key_insight: ApexGO is a generative AI system that redesigns peptide antibiotics to improve killing of drug‑resistant bacteria, producing candidates that match or outperform standard antibiotics in lab and mouse models.
problem_solved: Addresses the slow, costly, and combinatorially large search for effective peptide antibiotics against drug‑resistant bacteria by automating sequence redesign and prioritizing candidates with real biological activity.
method: Train a generative model (ApexGO) on peptide sequences and activity data to learn mappings from sequence to antimicrobial properties.
Use the model to propose redesigned peptide variants optimized for potency and other constraints (e.g., toxicity, stability).
Iteratively validate top in silico candidates with in vitro assays (MIC) and in vivo mouse infection models to confirm efficacy.
impact: Demonstrates that generative models can produce biologically validated therapeutic candidates, highlighting a scalable AI-driven workflow that shortens the design‑to‑validation cycle for peptide drug discovery and encourages tighter ML–wet‑lab integration.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: data → ApexGO generative model → candidate ranking → lab & mouse validation
Sequence space map: original vs. redesigned peptide clusters showing movement toward higher predicted activity
Bar charts: MIC/activity comparisons of top ApexGO peptides vs. standard antibiotics
Survival curve excerpt: mouse infection outcomes comparing treated vs. control groups
paper_title: A generative artificial intelligence approach for peptide antibiotic optimization
paper_authors: Marcelo D. T. Torres, Yimeng Zeng, Fangping Wan, Natalie Maus, Jacob Gardner
